info.title: LocalRun — rebuild and run only what matters locally: scan repositories,
info.description: Try a library change in the services that consume it as a NuGet package, across repositories: lrun scans them, builds the project dependency graph, repacks the libraries in between into a local feed in dependency order, and runs the executables side by side.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: track dependency graphs and repack components to a local NuGet source.

commands.name: build
commands.description: Scan a directory tree for projects and write their dependency graph to a config file.

options.name: --root
options.description: Directory to scan (default: current directory)

options.name: --local-nuget
options.description: Local NuGet feed to repack into (default: ~/.localnuget)

options.name: --config
options.description:
Config file to write (default: localrun.config.json)
Config file to read (default: localrun.config.json)

options.name: --users-of
options.description: Keep the given projects and all that depend on them, transitively

options.name: --deps-of
options.description:
Keep the given projects and all they depend on, transitively
With both: only the projects between them (AND)

options.name: --git-changes
options.description:
Add the projects with uncommitted changes or commits not on origin's
default branch to --users-of (compares with your last fetch)

options.name: --union
options.description: With both: users of --users-of OR deps of --deps-of

options.name: --with-services
options.description: Also keep the executables using any kept project, with the libraries in between

options.name: --include-external
options.description: Keep dependencies on projects that no solution references

options.name: --tests
options.description: Keep the test projects (left out by default)

options.name: --csproj
options.description:
Don't query your NuGet sources and local feed for the latest versions:
pack then starts from the csproj versions (default: from the latest)

options.name: --plot
options.description:
Then plot the graph, as 'plot' does with its defaults
plot [options]
Render the dependency graph of a config file as DOT and SVG.

options.name: --output
options.description: Output path without extension (default: lrun-visuals/dependencies-<date-time>)

options.name: --open
options.description:
Open the SVG with the default application
pack [options]
Plan what will be repacked and to which versions, and write it to a repack config.

options.name: --repack-config
options.description:
Repack config file to write (default: repack.config.json)
Repack config file to read (default: repack.config.json)
up [options]
Build the executables of a config file, then run them side by side; Ctrl+C stops them all.

options.name: --major
options.description: Increment major version (resets minor/patch)

options.name: --minor
options.description: Increment minor version (resets patch)

options.name: --patch
options.description: Increment patch version

options.name: --next
options.description: Continue a prerelease (1.5.0-alpha.9 -> 1.5.0-alpha.10), or patch a release

options.name: --alpha
options.description: Shorthand for --next --suffix alpha

options.name: --suffix
options.description:
Set the prerelease label, without the dash (default: local; e.g., 'dev', 'beta.2')
An iteration number follows it: 1.4.3-dev.1, then .2 when packed again

options.name: --clean
options.description: Clean projects before restoring them

options.name: --go
options.description:
Execute the plan right away, as 'go' does (default: only write it)
go [options]
Pack projects in dependency order into the local NuGet feed, following a repack config.

options.name: --exclude
options.description:
Executables not to run, e.g. the one you debug from your IDE
help
Show this help message.
version
Show the installed version (also --version). Please include it when reporting an issue.
